question: When governments legally obliged food producers to add extra nutrients to particular foods or categories of foods it is called ___________ .
solution:
The correct answer is __**food fortification.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Food fortification is the process of adding extra nutrients to particular foods or categories of foods to improve their nutritional value.**
 
• This is often done by governments to address nutrient deficiencies in the population, such as adding iodine to salt to prevent iodine deficiency disorders.
 
• **Food protection** refers to measures taken to **prevent food contamination or spoilage,** such as proper storage and handling practices.
 
• **Food adulteration i**s the addition of **harmful or inferior substances to food,** often for economic gain, and is illegal.
 
• **Food packaging **refers to the materials and** methods used to contain and protect food products during storage, transportation, and sale.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primordial prevention:** It is the first level of prevention and it aims at risk factor reduction towards an entire population through a focus on social and environmental conditions. The primordial prevention measures are promoted through national policies and laws. For example, National nutritional programs, ICDS, Mid-day meal programs, etc are providing nutritional supplements to the entire population to prevent mortality and morbidity rates in nutritional problems.
 
• **Secondary prevention:** It emphasizes early disease detection and its target is healthy-appearing individuals with subclinical forms of the disease. Secondary prevention occurs in the form of screenings.
 
• **Tertiary prevention:** It targets both clinical and outcome stages of a disease. It is implemented in symptomatic patients to reduce the severity of the disease as well as any associated sequelae. Forms of tertiary prevention are commonly rehabilitation service
